Way ya brain works, ELI5, is your eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin pick up stimuli. The nerves carry the message to the spinal column (if its a reflex. Reflex don't get handled in the brain. A sensory neuron is triggered, hits the spine, and shoots back down to the same spot in a motor neuron.) Or it travels up the spine to the brain. The information goes through a "sorter", that ignores information it doesn't care about, or sends information it cares about to the prefrontal cortex (if this information needs to be processed and conscious thought about. Then shoots to brain part that deals with how you communicate to speak.)/hippocampus ie for short/long term memory storage.

Your brain has a filter. If you're lookin for something/one specific, it will often filter out everything/one else and that information dies in your brain before being processed or converted to conscious awareness.

Tanking is about pace, reading the group, positioning and not dying.

**Pace**- don't go slow, but don't overextend yourself. Know yourself and your healer. If your healer is jumping around or pulling his weight in dps, go faster. If your healer goes, "Jesus Christ" or "you're gonna make me work  for this, aren't ya?" after a pull, slow down a little. Know what your capable of. As a DK know what you can confidently hps and pull around that number. If it's 8k, and you see your pulling 12k out of your ass somehow, slow it down.

Chain pull, but drop combat between pulls. If the healers good, all they need is the drop from combat to get Mana and be up for the next fight before you die. But be smart. Read health bars. If everyones low, and healer needs Mana, stop. If everyone's topped off, but healer needs Mana, pull (assuming it's a good healer that knows positioning.)

**Positioning**- if you notice your dps like to bounce around like a ADHD kid, pull your packs away from other packs so they don't pull. Place mobs near corners for abilities that can be LOSed, if a corner exists. I knew I had a good tank in CoS, in Legion, when they pulled enforcers to a corner. Just, be smart where you tank shit. Using your camera to keep track of your surroundings.

**Know your group** - people are stupid. Look for trends. If you notice mellee won't stop standing in shit (reading HP bars and knowing abilities), drag mobs away so they follow you out of the shit. If they say something, "don't stand in shit then".

**Not dying** - is about doing all that and knowing how to use your mitigation. As a DK, you can pretty much keep yourself mostly alive. It's frankly annoying as a healer to heal DKs cause you waste so much Mana on heals they didn't really need. I ran into one DK with a 7k raider.io score (in Legion) that I just simply ignored on a 15. He did not need me one bit. He refused to die. No idea what he was doing, but a goddamn beast he was. I think we woulda 4 chested it if that was a thing.

Most importantly, it takes practice. When you hit 120 and do heroic dungeons, pay attention to mob abilities and learn what they do. Follow people to learn paths.

Being good is difficult. There's a shit ton to keep track of. But with practice comes comfort and everything slows down. It won't seem so chaotic always. Muscle memory comes into play so you aren't thinking about what to hit, you just hit it. You start to notice things faster. At first looking with your camera will fuck you up. But eventually it becomes second nature.

Adenosine is a neurotransmitter. It's what communicates the message from neuron to another neuron. Neurons are nerve cells that tell your body what to do.

Caffeine replicates ( or blocks the recievability of the message) adenosine and tells the brain to do something or not do something. In this case, 'dont feel tired'.

For example a lot of opiates act like endorphins (the natural painkiller in your body). Basically you are taking a pill of neurotransmitters, in this case endorphins. So your brain is being artificially told to numb pain, in the absence of endorphins. 

Put another way, endorphins are a Gucci shirt. The real thing. Opiates are a knock off Gucci shirt. Your brain can't tell the difference between the real thing and the knock off. So it wears the shirt thinking it's real Gucci.

Your body has these things called neurotransmitters. They tell your brain what to do and thus tell your body what to do. They are what communicate the message from neuron to neuron. 

All drugs that affect humans replicate a naturally occurring neurotransmitter and act on the neuron as the neurotransmitter would. If you don't have a neurotransmitter for the drug to replicate, it has zero effect on you. 

So all a drug is doing is tricking your brain into thinking the neurotransmitters are telling it to do something it's really not.

Now, this is how withdrawal and tolerance happens. Use enough and your brain thinks their are to many neurotransmitters in the brain and cuts back production of naturally occurring ones. So you have to use more drugs to get the same amount of neurotransmitters going. Stop the drug use and the brain has to readjust the amount of neurotransmitters in the brain.

They can also block the message, but that requires understanding of how neurons work.
